The Pink Line Metro Bangalore is the most talked-about project in the city’s transport story. It is expected to change how people travel from south to north Bengaluru — making daily commutes faster, easier, and cheaper.

Key Takeaways

  • The Pink Line Metro Bangalore connects Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru to Nagawara in the north.
  • It will open in two phases in 2026 — elevated section first, then underground.
  • There are 18 stations, including major interchanges with other Namma Metro lines.
  • The line promises better connectivity, less traffic, and more travel choices for commuters.

What is the Pink Line Metro Bangalore?

The Pink Line will create a north-south spine that will connect the Namma Metro with a new corridor.

In simple words, it is a long metro route that:

  • Runs from Kalena Agrahara in the south to Nagawara in the north.
  • Covers about 21 km.
  • Has both elevated and underground sections.
  • Includes interchanges with other metro lines like Purple line metro , Yellow, Red, Orange, and Blue.

This new line is a big change for Bengaluru’s transport network, It connects far-flung areas and makes it easier to reach to offices, schools, hospitals, and the central business district.

Why the Pink Line Matters (Connectivity Impact)

Before the Pink Line opens, most people have to use the bus, car, or bike to travel over large distances across the city.

Here’s how the Pink Line changes things:

Benefits for Commuters:

  • Faster journeys compared to road traffic.
  • Easy access to IT parks, hospitals, schools, and business hubs.
  • Better option for students and office workers.
  • Fewer private vehicles on busy roads.

The daily transportation experience is more convenient and improved for riders because a metro runs on schedule and avoids road traffic.

 

Pink Line Route Map — Deep Diveh2)

Let’s break the route into two parts:

1. Elevated Section: Kalena Agrahara → Tavarekere

This part runs above the road — mainly along Bannerghatta Road — a key route in south Bengaluru.

Why it’s important:

  • This corridor connects many of the business districts in South Bangalore that see heavy traffic.
  • The residents in the region travel here for jobs, school, and/or shopping.

 

2. Underground Section: Tavarekere → Nagawara

This large portion goes below ground through central areas like MG Road and Shivajinagar.

Important points:

  • Passes under the city’s busiest zones.
  • Avoids road jams and keeps trains running on time.
  • Connects big commercial areas with residential parts and bus stands.

Underground metro lines take longer to build, but they give huge benefits in crowded cities like Bengaluru.

 

 

Launch Timeline: When Will the Pink Line Open?

Many people are excited and asking the same question: “When will the Pink Line start?”

Here is what I found on the most current project and construction schedule according to official sources:

📅 Expected Launch Dates

Phase

Section

Estimated Opening

Phase 1

Kalena Agrahara → Tavarekere (Elevated)

May 2026

Phase 2

Tavarekere → Nagawara (Underground)

Dec 2026

This phased launch is because:

  • Elevated section is easier to finish and test.
  • Underground tunnels take more time due to complex work.

According to experts, this is a plan that will allow commuters to begin using part of the railway line before work is completed on elsewhere.

 

 

What’s Happening in Construction Now?

The metro project has seen progress and delays over the years. Some sections were planned for earlier dates, but timelines changed.

Latest construction insights include:

  • Tunnelling work is mostly done for major underground parts.
  • Safety and signal tests are ongoing before final approval.
  • Prototype trains are being tested on tracks.

Once the line has been tested and certified as safe, also once approval is given, trains will be made available to transport passengers on a continuing basis.

Bangalore Metro Pink Line Timings (2026 Status)

Currently, as of 2026, the Pink Line of the Bengaluru Metro is still under construction. So, regular passenger train timings have not started yet.

However, BMRCL provided information regarding the planned operating hours of the Pink Line after it is opened to the public in 2026.

Latest News Updates on Bangalore Metro Pink Line Extension

The Pink Line Metro Bangalore is part of Phase-2 of Namma Metro.

Latest Official Updates (2025)

  • Elevated section from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere will open first
  • Expected launch: May 2026
  • Underground section from Tavarekere to Nagawara will open by December 2026
  • Train trials and safety checks are in progress

Conclusion

The Pink Line Metro Bangalore is more than just a new metro route. It is a major step toward making Bengaluru a better, faster, and more liveable city.

By connecting south Bangalore's Kalena Agrahara with north Bangalore's Nagawara, the Pink Line creates a significant amount of time savings, decreases congestion on our city streets, and creates an excellent daily travel option for our citizens.

The Pink line has 18 stations throughout the city, with several locations where you can change trains, as well as low-cost fares and making it the best way to get to work, school, home, or to take family members on outings for all citizens.

FAQs on Namma Metro Pink Line Bangalore

1)What is the status of Pink Line metro in Bangalore?

As of the beginning of 2026, Bengaluru's Pink Metro Line was still under construction. Several tests were performed and were still undergoing safety checks. It is expected to open for public use starting in phases in 2026.

2)Is Bengaluru's Pink Line metro line set to be ready by 2026?

Yes, The first phase of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to be opened in May of 2026. The second phase of the underground section of the Pink Line is expected to be opened in December of 2026.

3)Which metro line is going to Bangalore airport?

The Blue Line Metro will connect Kempegowda International Airport to the city. It will run from KR Puram to the airport via Hebbal and Nagawara

4)Is Bangalore Metro Pink Line open?

No, the Bangalore Metro Pink Line is not open yet. It is still under construction and is expected to start operations in phases in 2026
